# Introduction

This file is used to conduct ordinal regression analysis on the survey responses of Recreational fishers from the SELTMP in 2025. Regressions test trends between support for MPAs against responses to other survey questions and demographics

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# R Setup & housekeeping
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
	echo = TRUE,
	include = TRUE,
	message = FALSE,
	warning = FALSE)

rm(list=ls())
objects()
```

```{r}
# Packages
library("gert")
library("usethis")
library("here")
library("tidyverse")
library("readxl")
library("ordinal")
library("rcompanion")
library("emmeans")
library("rms")
```

```{r}
# Import Raw Data sheet
raw_data <- read_excel(here::here("Data/SELTMP-2025-GBR-surveydataset_v1-0_RecFishingCLUSTERS_RyanW-Sept-22-2026.xlsx"), sheet = "Raw_Data")

##glimpse(raw_data)
```

```{r}
# Filter Data for only Rec Fishers
fisher_data <- raw_data |>
  filter(!is.na(inter_zoning), Are_you_a_Rec_Fisher == "Y")
```

## Test Assumptions

### Pearson's Test (Goodness of Fit)

```{r}
# Switch variables to numeric for test
fisher_data$inter_zoning <- as.numeric(as.character(fisher_data$inter_zoning))
fisher_data$educ         <- as.numeric(as.character(fisher_data$educ))

cor.test(fisher_data$inter_zoning, fisher_data$educ)
```

### Alternative: Spearman's Test (rank based)

```{r}
cor.test(fisher_data$inter_zoning, fisher_data$educ, method = "spearman", exact = FALSE)
```

### Scatter plot

```{r}
# Help visualize trends based on responses
ggplot(data = fisher_data, aes(x = inter_zoning, y = educ)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.25, height = 0.25, alpha = 0.3, size = 1.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:7) +
  labs(x = "Importance of marine park zoning (1-10)",
       y = "Education level (1-7)") 
```

### Multicollinearity (VIF)

```{r}
# VIF test needs multiple variables

# Can add in multiple predictors under one variable   
q14 <- c("GBRbp_advocacyfish", "GBRbp_rubbish", "GBRbp_app", "GBRbp_report")

# Q14 has a "9" response for "not applicable" that needs to be converted to NA 
fisher_data[q14] <- lapply(fisher_data[q14], function(x) ifelse(x == 9, NA, x))

# Transform variables to numeric for VIF test
vif_data <- fisher_data |> 
  transmute( 
    inter_zoning = as.numeric(as.character(inter_zoning)),
    educ = as.numeric(as.character(educ)),
    across(all_of(q14), ~ as.numeric(as.character(.x)))
  ) |>
  
  # Omit Na Values
  na.omit()

# list how many respondents are actually usable
nrow(vif_data)

# Run test (dependent variable first, then predictors)
m_vif <- ols(inter_zoning ~ educ + GBRbp_advocacyfish + GBRbp_rubbish +
               GBRbp_app + GBRbp_report,
             data = vif_data)

rms::vif(m_vif)   
```

### Test the proportional odds assumption

```{r}
# Set up dependent variable as factor or numerical
fisher_data <- fisher_data |>
 mutate(inter_zoning = factor(inter_zoning, ordered = TRUE)) |>

# Set up predictor variable(s) to run regression against
  mutate(educ = factor(educ, levels = 1:7, ordered = FALSE)      # use for categorical question
# mutate(a = numeric(a))      # use for numeric question
  ) |>
  drop_na(educ)
```

```{r}
# Change column to to numerical binary for test
fisher_data |>
  mutate(Fisher_numeric = ifelse(Are_you_a_Rec_Fisher == "Recreational Fisher", 1, 0))

# Set up model (can add in other predictors w/ +)
ord_reg <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = fisher_data, link = "logit")

# Test for violation of proportional odds
nominal_test(ord_reg)

# Plot results
plot.xmean.ordinaly(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = fisher_data, cr = TRUE)
```

## Run ordinal regression model

### One Predictor
```{r}
# Set up dependent and predictor variables
clm_data <- fisher_data |>
  select(inter_zoning, educ)|>
  na.omit()

# Outcome must be an ordered factor; predictors can be numeric or factor/categorical
clm_data <- clm_data |>
  mutate(inter_zoning = factor(inter_zoning, ordered = TRUE),
         educ = as.numeric(as.character(educ)))

# Sample Size
nrow(clm_data)

# One predictor
ord_educ <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ, data = clm_data, link = "logit")
summary(ord_educ)
```

### Multiple Predictors
```{r}
# Set up dependent and predictor variables
q14 <- c("GBRbp_advocacyfish", "GBRbp_rubbish", "GBRbp_app", "GBRbp_report")

clm_data <- fisher_data |>
  select(inter_zoning, educ, q14)|>
  na.omit()

# Outcome must be an ordered factor; predictors can be numeric or factor/categorical
clm_data <- clm_data |>
  mutate(inter_zoning = factor(inter_zoning, ordered = TRUE),
         educ = as.numeric(as.character(educ)),
         across(all_of(q14), ~ as.numeric(as.character(.x))))

# Sample Size
nrow(clm_data)
# Multiple predictors
ord_full <- clm(inter_zoning ~ educ + GBRbp_advocacyfish + GBRbp_rubbish + GBRbp_app + GBRbp_report,
                data = clm_data, link = "logit")
summary(ord_full)
```
